//scripts._: What each script does. These notes used to sit inside the command strings as trailing "# …" comments, which made the shell discard any arguments passed after "--" (so a gate given --url silently measured its hardcoded default port — possibly another agent's server). Keep notes here, never in a command.
//scripts.browser-gates: lists every package.json script that launches a browser (the same detection run-parallel uses to route them through internal/browser-slot.sh). Run each as internal/browser-slot.sh bun run <name>.
//scripts.cap:sync: NOT `bunx` — bunx is not on PATH in this environment (command not found, exit 127), which broke cap:sync -> apk:debug -> phone at step one. The CLI IS installed locally (@capacitor/cli 7.6.9); invoke the local bin directly. The rest of package.json already uses the spaced `bun x` form.
//scripts.capability-exemplars: regenerate documentation/reference-capability-exemplars.md — the DERIVED answer to "which bundle is the capability-N example?", a question answered WRONGLY in three separate artifacts (a gate, the README, the /plugin-designer skill).
//scripts.check:a11y-button-names: every VISIBLE button must have an accessible name (aria-label / aria-labelledby / visible text — a `title` is a TOOLTIP and does NOT count). Measures the RENDERED DOM through shadow roots: a source grep cannot answer this (132 `<button>` hits, most with visible text). Needs a browser, so NOT in build:unlocked and NOT in CI. ALL=1 sweeps every profile.
//scripts.check:mobile-gating: the SPA device rules stay on their shelves: DESKTOP_ONLY ids are curated production tabs (blocked on a narrow screen, disabled + a message naming the map), MOBILE_NOTICE ids are Experimental bundles (they open on a narrow screen with a dismissible not-built-for-mobile notice), the predicates read their set + narrow, and all 11 locales carry the four strings. Headless; --self-test proves each rule can fail.
//scripts.check:approx-pin-note: people-group pins say they are localities, not towns or boundaries, in ONE shared wording (library/components/legends/ApproxPinNote.vue): the colocation index finds groups sharing a coordinate, the note names them only for a shared point, never prints a raw coordinate, and renders from each locale's catalogue. Headless.
//scripts.check:auto-engine: BROWSER. The default engine is auto: on one map leaf, no token draws with MapLibre and makes zero api.mapbox.com requests, a token draws with Mapbox, and an explicit provider wins. Under the fleet browser policy it is a rega run, not part of gates:post.
//scripts.check:plural-forms: the three things a CLDR pluralRules map can silently break. (1) FORM COUNT: a locale must author as many forms as it has CLDR categories or the pick clamps onto the wrong one (ru 4, ar 6). (2) THE tStatic PATH: seven bundles install no vue-i18n and read through tStatic, which does NO plural selection, so a pipe key there reaches the page as the literal "a | b | c". (3) ZERO: a locale with an explicit CLDR zero category must author it. Written as the precondition for installing the map, and kept as the guard after.
//scripts.check:backlog-refs: a card may not depend on a card that does not exist. A dangling depends_on can never be done, so the card can never become ready and nothing says so — it reads as ordinary blocked work forever. FAILS only for depends_on on an OPEN card; a dangling parent or a stale link on a done card is REPORTED, because failing on filing debt teaches people to delete the reference rather than restore the card. Reads all three phase backlogs — references legitimately cross phases. SKIPs when _qa-cycle is absent.
//scripts.check:basemap-labels: the BASEMAP's place names follow the reader's language on BOTH engines (library/maps/localize-labels.js): reads the RENDERED country labels at ?lang=en and ?lang=ru — Mapbox via the Standard basemap's place-labels featureset, MapLibre via each symbol's evaluated text — and requires them to flip. Serves this checkout on an OS-assigned port; --dir <tree> for a negative control. Negative-tested: a bundle built before 319064a1 FAILS on both engines.
//scripts.check:browser-gates-guarded: no repo file imports playwright except through internal/lib/playwright-guarded.mjs, whose launch refuses (exit 75, NOT MEASURED) unless internal/browser-slot.sh has exported DOXA_BROWSER_SLOT. Browsers run only on the browser seat, inside the slot; this makes that rule enforced, not remembered.
//scripts.check:capability-citations: a doc that names a bundle as "capability N" must match manifest.json, which is what the BUILD computed. README captioned doxa-vision-card as cap-1; it ships 2 instances so it is parameterized (cap-2). The SAME error was fixed once in verify-5-capabilities.mjs and never reached the README — two copies of one fact, nothing forcing agreement.
//scripts.check:capability-derived: every bundle lands on a real capability 1-5, never 0, and a DECLARED tier must agree with the composes edges it declares. Tiers 3-5 used to be authored only - discover.mjs infers single and parameterized and nothing else - so a composite whose author forgot a meta.json shipped as capability 1; research-dashboard did exactly that while nesting ten views, and a missing file is indistinguishable from a deliberate choice, so nothing failed. The declaration stays authoritative: it is CHECKED, not overridden, because a meta that contradicts the structure means one of the two is stale and picking silently is how a tier rots. Two traps found by running the rule BEFORE writing it: composes is per-PROFILE at source but hoisted to the BUNDLE in the manifest, so deriving from the bundle row gave a composite's edges to its plain sibling leaves (11 false failures on correct data); and refs come in two forms in one field, 'bundle/profile' and a bare 'bundle', so resolving only the first demoted plugin-studio from 5 to 4. With both handled: 10 composing profiles, 10 agree, 0 disagree. An unresolved ref is REPORTED, never counted as 'not a composite' - a typo and a genuine plain child look identical from here. Negative-tested on the research-dashboard shape (a composite declared single).
//scripts.check:capability-exemplars: REGENERATES and content-compares (not mtimes: a full build rewrites manifest.json every time, so an mtime rule would cry wolf after every build and get switched off).
//scripts.check:catalog-identity: proves the LIVE server serves the CATALOG’s exact bytes, by hashing each live bundle and comparing sha384 against the manifest’s own integrity field. An HTTP 200 cannot do this: /app/doxa-maps/ returns 200 with a 2872-byte HTML SIGN-IN PAGE. Network-dependent, so NOT in build:unlocked and NOT in CI; SKIPs cleanly when unreachable. CATALOG=<dir> also requires the live manifest to match a catalog checkout.
//scripts.check:cdn-cache: the container's /cdn cache headers, over real HTTP against a server it starts on 127.0.0.1: moving files (manifest, runtime config, html, bundle entries) max-age=300, hashed names a year + immutable, other assets an hour; every response has an ETag and answers If-None-Match with 304. By the repo owner. Headless; in gates:pre.
//scripts.check:cdn-pins: every runtime third-party script/stylesheet in shipped code is an exact version listed in library/constants/cdn.js with its SRI hash (no floating ranges). --online re-fetches each and compares the hash.
//scripts.check:click-sheet: the COUNTRY-CLICK SHEET without a GPU: every country in the roster resolves to >=1 pin, every link the sheet would render is absolute, and has_audio stays the STRING "unknown" where the pool was never checked (collapsing it to false would read as "no audio exists"). It had been CRASHING on a path deleted when data moved out of public/, and its two inputs were a private by-country copy and the curated 2,106-row subset the sheet stopped reading — so it was unrunnable AND aimed at files the surface no longer uses. Joins by ISO3 now, not by country-name substring. Carries its own 4-case self-test. Static, sub-second.
//scripts.check:composed-filters: CELL C — the gospel map composed above its own tables. Asserts the composite keeps the reader INSIDE it: "Every resource in <language>" must be a <button> that filters in place, not an <a> that navigates away and throws out the map the reader just positioned. Checks the tag, that the URL did not change, that the table NARROWED (row count down but not to zero), that the pin count survived, and that nothing 4xx'd. Picks a tier-2 pin from the live source — the first version opened pin 0, a group with nothing found, and failed a working composite on an empty table. Browser gate: run under both rendezvous locks, product lock first.
//scripts.check:composite: a COMPOSITE is a COPY taken at its own build time: fails if a nested child's source is newer than the parent's bundle. NOT in build:unlocked on purpose — there everything was just built, so it could never catch the real case (a PARTIAL build). Run it before PUBLISH.
//scripts.check:composite-embed-knobs: a composite must pass the HOST's tk and provider down to the map it nests, proven on a genuinely foreign origin (tree served on one port, partner page on another). Our own leaves bake a token and assign window.MAP_TOKEN, so this only ever breaks where there is no leaf - the partner page the embed snippet is written for, and the case nothing else tested. Keyless maplibre asserts ZERO requests to api.mapbox.com, because 'it rendered' would pass on a build that quietly fell back with a baked key.
//scripts.check:clustering-modes: every option in the research map's clustering picker must DRAW something different. Choosing 'Native' changed nothing: mapStore never declared clusteringMode, so the picker wrote to a property nothing watched, AND the Clusters checkbox force-set 'mst' regardless of the store, so even a fixed picker would have snapped back on the next tick. Asserts on what the GL style RENDERS (circles, count labels, lines), not on state - 'clusteringMode === mapbox' would pass on a build still drawing MST. Also asserts no orphan layers between modes, and that MST and Network differ, since two labels for one behaviour is the same defect as a dead option.
//scripts.check:composite-interop: every link between a capability-4 composite's children exists on BOTH ends, headless: the event, attribute or config-key name is sent in the sender file and listened for in the receiver (a rename on one side fails, naming both files), the same literal is in every built bundle that ships an end, every composite is mapped (or says why it has no links), and no host lookup calls getCurrentInstance() inside a plain function, where Vue returns null when it runs from a watcher. Exists because Simple Research map -> grid died that way while a synthetic-event proof passed. Both ends existing is necessary, not sufficient: the runtime half is check:gallery-embed's linked phase.
//scripts.check:composite-locale-leaks: a composite rendered in a non-English locale must not show a string the catalogue already translates. The criterion is a LOOKUP, not a category: English catalogue holds the string as a value, this locale holds a different value for that key, the page still renders English. The previous sweep split strings into chrome/data/third-party and scored single words like 'Region' and 'Prayer' as data, so 28 leaks on Big Picture and 41 on Simple Research counted as zero. Surfaces that a lookup cannot judge - vendor map chrome, table DATA cells, facet-rail values - are suppressed by NAME with a stated reason, never by word.
//scripts.check:composite-token-url: a composite embedded BARE (no outer ProfileLoader) must honour a tokenUrl-only config: it reads tokenUrl, forwards it, and asks the token service only when no token is given. The expectation is derived from ProfileLoader, not restated. Headless; in gates:pre.
//scripts.check:composites-mount: every capability-4/5 composite's OWN setup() and mounted hooks run without throwing, in en and ar, headless (no browser): vite loads each composite as its bundle entry defines it (configureApp, and ProfileLoader's provides where the entry mounts ProfileLoader), and @vue/runtime-core mounts it on a no-op renderer. Exists because 08f89f55 shipped two composites calling getRuntimeLocale/detectLocale/RTL_LOCALES with no import: the build was green, setup threw a ReferenceError in every locale, and Big Picture and Simple Research rendered nothing. Proves setup runs; cannot prove the children render.
//scripts.check:coverage-consistent: the gospel-resources surfaces must agree: no resource on an ISO RESERVED code (und/mul/mis/zxx), every resourced code NAMED, table reach recounted off the pins, no invented URL, tiers reconcile. Static, sub-second. Self-test: `bun run check:coverage-consistent:poison`, all 12 clauses (A-L) must fail. Clause L is the one that is not about consistency: it fails when the link-verification record goes stale, because 'link checked' is a claim about the present tense. Written after the same drift defect was found by hand three times.
//scripts.check:csv-shape: the export must OPEN as a table: header on line 0, every row matching. Run the `check:csv-shape:self-test` script for the NEGATIVE test (forces the provenance comment back to line 0 IN MEMORY and requires this gate to REJECT it) — the header used to claim 'NEGATIVE-TESTED' with no way to re-run it.
//scripts.check:dashboard-filter-a11y: the dashboard's cross-filter is operable and audible: every filter chip is a <button type="button"> with an aria-label naming the ACTION (a filter that can be set by keyboard must be clearable by keyboard), the shell carries exactly ONE always-rendered polite role="status" region so a brush that changes a number far from the control is announced once rather than six times or not at all, and no resize handle's accessible name is a raw English literal. AST over the parsed templates plus the built bundle — no browser (rega's alone).
//scripts.check:dashboard-geocoder-provider: the research dashboard leaf at ?provider=maplibre makes ZERO requests to api.mapbox.com, and its search bars still suggest (built tree; browser gate). It was kept out of gates:post while the generated leaf hard-linked the Mapbox engine; the leaf now loads only the engine it is asked for.
//scripts.check:dep-names: every declared dep is a REAL package name (a rename once rewrote @capacitor/* and broke bun install in a clone)
//scripts.check:describe-group: the prayer packet's generated profile sentence (library/packets/describeGroup.js): each GSEC level states its own fact, and an index-ordered language name ("Arabic, Moroccan") is un-inverted by library/utils/languageLabel.js without shredding a comma inside parentheses, the 13 names the old split printed reversed. A catalogue arm renders every GSEC level from the REAL packet-strings.json in en and ar and fails on a blank sentence. Headless; in gates:pre.
//scripts.check:descriptions: every shipped profile must say what it is (reads the BUILT manifest)
//scripts.check:done-evidence: a card may not reach status:done with NO bluf AND NO fields — the Doxa team inherits this board and an evidence-less 'done' cannot be reconciled against the code. 10 pre-existing are baselined by id; the list should only ever SHRINK.
//scripts.check:dxlife: ⚠ NOT WAVE-SAFE, deliberately unwired: exit codes 0/1/2 are a DOCUMENTED contract (0 unchanged · 1 drift · 2 clone not found), and run-parallel grades any non-zero as FAILURE — so a checkout without the sibling /root-dx-life clone goes red on a precondition. Changing the contract could break another consumer; hand-run it, or give it a recognised SKIP first.
//scripts.check:element-census-vs-live: what is on ONE side and not the other, ours vs the live doxa.life page we clone: harvests every visible TEXT NODE through every shadow root on both sides and diffs the SETS. OURS-ONLY unaccounted = a scope violation (FAIL), THEIRS-ONLY = a clone omission (FAIL), SANCTIONED = an allowlist entry carrying the Driver's words + date + card (refused without them), DATA DRIFT = same label, different digits (reported). The negative control is MANDATORY: a known ours-only string must land in the ours-only set or it prints CENSUS IS BLIND and exits 75; an unreachable live page is also 75. Presets: internal/element-census/<name>.json (--preset <name>, default all); ad hoc: --leaf <bundle/profile/index.html[#hash]> --live <url> --neg <text> [--sanctioned <file>]. Promoted from regions' probe; regions passes (list 229 vs 228, the only difference its sanctioned poster toggle). Through browser-slot.sh.
//scripts.check:embed-base: the shared URL resolver, pinned by ARITHMETIC — no browser, no network, no served tree, so it cannot SKIP itself into irrelevance. It computes what a leaf's own "../../assets" means and asserts the resolver agrees. Caught nothing for fifteen ticks because it did not exist: resolveAssetsBase computed one segment too high, every local gate passed (the dev web-root has assets BOTH inside and beside the tree), and the byte-level publish gates went green on the broken publish.
//scripts.check:embed-basemap: the gospel map's BASEMAP must paint inside a genuinely cross-origin iframe on the token the page BAKES, not one a probe forces on it. Every other browser gate here forces a restricted token (u=doxalife) that 403s on the basemap, then counts PINS — which come from our own GeoJSON and paint with no token at all — so 'the map renders' had never been measured. Runs a negative control every time by rewriting the token on the wire; if the control passes it reports PROVED NOTHING rather than a pass. ~60s, needs a browser.
//scripts.check:embed-targets: every embed.iframe src in manifest.json must resolve to a file that EXISTS. Those snippets ARE deployment-method 1 (iframe) — a partner pastes them verbatim — and NOTHING else asserts their targets are still emitted, because every other gate walks only files that exist and is blind to ABSENCE. `the `check:embed-targets:self-test` script` poisons a copy of the manifest and asserts the gate NOTICES: a gate that cannot fail is worse than no gate.
//scripts.check:embedder-keys: regions-mfe forwards page-scoped config to its nested panes by an explicit key list (INHERITED_PAGE_KEYS). Asserts the documented embedder keys travel (dataSource, tokenUrl among them) AND that profile and instanceId do NOT: the host's would overwrite each pane's own and collapse both tabs into one view.
//scripts.check:english-leaks: A translated key must not render in English. rega's method: a string is a LEAK when the catalogue has a DIFFERENT value for the locale and the page still shows the English one - a render/wiring fault, not a missing translation. Third-party attributions, data names, placeholder-only strings and the prose this bundle deliberately keeps in English are all excluded, the last by simply not being in the catalogue. Scoped to the LEAF on purpose: six keys were reported leaking in the gallery and the leaf is clean in ar/zh/ru/hi - the gallery builds its iframe src with no lang parameter, so the embed never learns the locale. Embedder defect, not a bundle one.
//scripts.check:experimental-shelf: Every Experimental-folder bundle, leaf + Gallery tab, mapbox + maplibre: mounts with content, 0 errors / failed requests, maps load and DRAW their own data. Self-tests on a deliberately broken bundle first. Run through internal/browser-slot.sh.
//scripts.check:export-poster-prints: the Simple Research 'Export poster' button opens the PRINT DIALOG on the poster in ONE click and downloads NOTHING (the Driver's rule, 2026-09-28): leaf AND Research Gallery, en AND ar; the printing document is the 1700x2200 poster on an 8.5in x 11in sheet; no download arrives; 0 page errors. window.print is stubbed, so this measures everything up to the dialog. //scripts.check:export-poster-prints:maplibre: the same four one-click prints on the keyless MapLibre engine (OpenFreeMap tiles): the hidden print map must be built with the engine that drew the screen, and the footer must credit the tiles actually printed.
//scripts.check:facet-cascade: a child facet selection must not outlive its parent: clearing a parent facet must cascade-clear its descendants on EVERY clear path. Asserts on RESULT COUNTS, not DOM — an orphaned child silently ANDs the map to empty. run check:facet-cascade:self-test for the NEGATIVE test (reverts the cascade and requires this gate to FAIL).
//scripts.check:facet-changes-map: a facet selection must CHANGE THE DOTS — and the dots must SAY what they mean. Asserts (1) the rd-bubbles feature set changes by count AND identity, (2) every surviving dot satisfies the selected level, (3) while a prayer filter is active circle-color is a DATA-DRIVEN EXPRESSION reading peoplePraying, not a flat literal. Assertion 3 is the one that matters: the prayer filter ALREADY narrowed 2107->689 correctly while the Driver reported it broken, because every dot painted the same orange. Browser gate (needs `bun run dev` on 5173, or BASE_URL/PROBE_PATH at a served tree), so NOT in build:unlocked. run the `check:facet-changes-map:self-test` script for the NEGATIVE test.
//scripts.check:facet-changes-map:built: the SAME gate against the BUILT tree instead of the dev server. Measured 2026-09-24: the dev default is 1 PASS / 3 FAIL in four runs on a busy box (88 unbundled module requests vs the built leaf's 3), while the built tree passes deterministically. Use this when you need a trustworthy answer; use the dev default when checking uncommitted source.
//scripts.check:facet-changes-map:self-test: reverts the fix IN THE LIVE PAGE and requires the gate to FAIL. SELF_TEST_MODE=colour (default, isolates the colour assertion — the reported bug) | props | both | frozen (blocks the source update, isolating the set assertion). All four modes verified caught.
//scripts.check:facet-one-field: ONE AXIS = ONE CONTROL-REACHABLE FACET. Asserts on the PARTITION each facet induces over the rows, NOT on which r.<field> it reads: three fields (religion, primary_language, rop1) are legitimately read by two facets each as tier-1/tier-2 pairs, so a gate on duplicate field READS would fail correct code. Scoped to facets a user can actually select (rail + dropdowns + charts), because a search-only projection sharing a partition is fine until it becomes a control. run check:facet-one-field:self-test for the NEGATIVE test.
//scripts.check:filter-multivalue: SPEC-DASHBOARD-KIT D1: filterSet[key] may hold an array meaning OR-within-key, keys still AND together — and exactly ONE function answers 'does this row match'. The rule `a(r) === filterSet[k]` was written out SEVEN times (shell, facet rail x2, map panel, table, charts rail, CSV exporter); the moment it grew an array case, six copies would have kept comparing an array with === , matched nothing, and left the panels disagreeing about what is on screen — the facet rail printing counts for a scope the map and table no longer render. Runs the real bus (OR within, AND across, one-element array collapses to a scalar, EMPTY array clears rather than matching nothing, toggleFilterValue adds/removes/clears, cascade intact), greps the panels for surviving copies, round-trips the URL hash including a value containing a comma, and lifts the grid's valueMatches to prove both ends OR the same way. The list separator is `|` and not `,` because 120 of the 864 live language labels contain a comma. No browser.
//scripts.check:fits-screen: THE FITNESS-FOR-USE GATE (LL-the-user-found-three-bugs-my-gates-could-not-see): a green STATE suite (mounts/fetches/counts/paints) said nothing about whether the product is USABLE, and the Driver found five real defects in one sitting that no gate saw. Asserts 5 clauses on the built dashboard-plus-grid composite + research-dashboard leaf, real browser, live data: (A) the dashboard band fits ONE 1440x900 viewport and is shorter than its own tree-legend's scrollHeight; (B) the people-groups grid is still reachable by scrolling underneath it (a fix for A must not re-break this — AP-fixing-reachability-by-making-the-thing-taller); (C) a wheel over the map changes ZOOM and does not scroll the pane, a wheel below it scrolls and does not zoom — instrumented on the DISPATCHED EVENT (composedPath), not geometry, per LL-four-wrong-diagnoses-instrument-the-event-not-the-geometry; (D) the grid's live count ([data-table-count], the composite's documented single source of truth — show-total=false on the grid child is deliberate) is visible and CHANGES when a facet narrows it; (E) a 1440/1280/768/390 responsive sweep has no horizontal document overflow and no element clipped to zero height (.rd-td/.rd-th ellipsis excluded — expected). Spawns its own serve-strict on PORT (default 4391); SKIPs (exit 0) if the tree is not settled at START OR re-settled at END, or pray.doxa.life is unreachable — never reports a defect from a torn tree. Also best-effort probes any cap-5 shell the manifest declares (type nested-mfe-spa) by CONTENT-MATCHING a tab, never by hardcoded structure, so it survives the shell's own in-flight restructure without depending on it. Needs a built tree (`bun run build`). run `check:fits-screen:self-test` for the NEGATIVE test.

//scripts.check:hover-channel: SPEC-DASHBOARD-KIT D3: the bus's third coordinated channel points at a record without committing to one. Runs the real bus: hover holds its own ref, never enters the selection, never bumps the version, never touches the filters, a repeat emits once (hover fires on every mousemove across 2,107 rows), and the three channels clear independently. //scripts.check:i18n-keys-exist: every literal catalogue key named in code exists in library/i18n/locales/en/. A localized CALL SITE is not a localized STRING: the dashboard's five resize handles all read T('aria.resizeFiltersRail', ...) and look correct in review, while aria.json held eleven keys and not one was a resize key - so every handle announced itself in English in all eleven locales, and the fallback that makes a missing key degrade to readable English is exactly what kept it silent. No other gate asks this: i18n-parity is satisfied because the key is missing from ALL locales equally, and english-leaks and composite-locale-leaks both need the catalogue to HOLD the string before an appearance counts as a leak. Matches tStatic/$t/t and the house-pattern T( alias, all of which take a full dotted key; prefix helpers like L( and any concatenated or template-literal key are COUNTED as unresolved and never guessed at. Found 22 missing keys on its first run. ROUND 2, after go-int planted T('poison_key') behind `const T = useGiT()` and this gate reported the tree CLEAN -- the one failure a check is not forgiven, because a red gate gets fixed and a green one that should be red gets believed. THREE independent blindnesses stacked, and any one alone hid the key: the file never writes the word tStatic so the precondition skipped it before anything ran; useGiT is not tStatic so no alias was found; and the alias is PREFIXED (useOptionalT carries a namespace) while its call sites pass BARE keys, which the full-key pattern cannot match because it requires a dot. Now a translator that arrives from a COMPOSABLE is resolved like any other, with the namespace READ from the factory's one-line body rather than listed here -- useOptionalT/useOptionalI18n directly, plus any `export function useXxxT() { return useOptionalT('ns') }`, which is how useNeighborT and usePplrT are written. Because qualify() prefixes a bare key and leaves an already-qualified one alone, one binding registers as BOTH shapes. MEASURED before and after with the same poison on disk: the old version PASSES it, this one fails it as 'neighbor.zzz_not_a_real_key (via nt())'; coverage went 683 -> 743 full-key and 49 -> 56 prefixed call sites, so 67 sites were being scored clean without being read. A self-test now asserts all three fixes separately and exits 3 if any goes blind, because this gate guards goal (d) and had already been trusted once while lying. Empty-namespace bare keys stay outside the model and are COUNTED rather than assumed away; measured at zero today, since all five such sites pass dotted keys.

A hoisted function promises that its NAME resolves early, not that its BODY can run early, and that asymmetry is invisible from both ends. ARM B: a lifecycle registrar closes over Vue's current instance, which exists only while setup is on the stack, so `onMounted(async () => { await init(); onBeforeUnmount(clean) })` drops the registration silently - DashboardMapPanel.vue leaked a ResizeObserver on document.body plus a window listener, warning only, feature working, and research-map.vue had a second copy this gate found. The fix is never 'move the line': declare the handle at setup scope and tear it down in a hook registered before the first await. Its own false positives are the interesting part - it went 6 hits -> 1 over three rounds, and every one it dropped was prose or shadowing read as code: `onBeforeUnmount` inside a console.error STRING, `table` inside `new Error(`table not found (${r.status})`)` in four files, and a `const [pins, byCountry]` destructured INSIDE the function, shadowing a computed 220 lines away. So it blanks comments, string text and template text (keeping ${...}, which is code) and subtracts every name a span declares for itself. Self-tests on both shipped defects, both fixes, and all three decoys; exits 3 if any arm goes blind.

//scripts.packet-fixture: regenerate the committed records subset (smallest zone, image_url stripped) that lets CI build a packet at all — out/ is gitignored, so a clean checkout has neither the records cache nor any packet.
//scripts.packet:ci: build EVERY committed fixture, no network, each renamed to its own output so they coexist. Was one fixture (tibet); packet.mjs names its output for the ZONE not the fixture, so sequential builds overwrote each other and check:packets-all saw a single SHAPE while reporting success. The fixtures are chosen at the PER_PAGE=20 page boundary — exactly 20, 21, and 1 group — because laos (95) and tibet (43) are both mid-range remainder cases and the boundary itself had never rendered.
//scripts.packets: the prayer packets. READS out/posters/<zone>.html for page 1's map, which `bun run posters` writes — without it the packet still builds and page 1 is simply BLANK, so the script now warns per-zone AND in its summary. PACKET_LANG=<loc> for one language, ONLY=<zoneKey> for one zone, NOPHOTOS=1 to skip the photo fetch. ENV: ONLY=<zone> one zone · PACKET_LANG=<locale> · PACKET_RECORDS=<file> a committed fixture instead of the live API · PACKET_LIST=<list-id> the universal list prop for this generator (doxa default; unreached/frontier/frontier-500k/unengaged read data/people-groups/lists/<id>.json from disk, since there is no server to fetch the asset pool from). PACKET_LIST FAILS CLOSED on an unknown or empty list rather than silently printing every group — a packet that showed the wrong list is printed and handed to someone. It exists because the browser path honours ?list= while this generator did not, so the six-row funnel (a list's own total inserted before the reader's row) was unreachable by the only pipeline that can render it.
//scripts.serve: serves public/ the way PRODUCTION does: a DIRECTORY request returns 404, no index fallback. This was python3 -m http.server, which DID resolve a directory to index.html while the live static layer does not — so gates passed on URLs that 404 live (measured 2026-09-23; it cost a false "publish failed" reading and hid a bad URL in verify-shell-scroll for a whole flight). Loopback only, same as before. Override port/host with PORT/HOST.
//scripts.serve:permissive: LOOPBACK ONLY. This was --bind 0.0.0.0, which published the built tree on every interface of whatever machine ran a gate; measured on the build VPS it answered HTTP 200 on the box's PUBLIC IP while a browser gate was running. Every consumer (verify-browser-all, check:a11y-button-names, check:nav-reachable, smoke:share-all) already defaults to 127.0.0.1, so nothing needed the wider bind. Override with BASE_URL/BASE if you deliberately want to reach it from another host.
//scripts.serve:shell: LOOPBACK ONLY, same reason as `serve` above — a local preview server has no business answering on a public interface.

//scripts.verify:interop: the CAP-4 INTEROPERABILITY GATE (real browser, real shadow DOM, real live data) — closes the gap verify:gate1 leaves open. Drives the ACTUAL compiled composites: (1) DESKTOP dashboard-plus-grid map->grid (a facet-rail click must narrow the grid's live `Showing N` count line — card count is a proven FALSE-NEGATIVE trap, always 24, never asserted on), (2) DESKTOP grid->map (selecting table rows must MOVE THE CAMERA, read back off window.__rdashMap.getCenter()/getZoom() — useSelectionCamera.js's contract), (3) MOBILE research-map-plus-grid, where source-reading FIRST established there is NO cross-wire between the map and grid children by design (StackLayout composes two independent elements, no provide/inject/prop crosses the boundary) — so this pair asserts each half narrows on its OWN control, not a link that does not exist. Prints ONE line per combination, pass/fail only, plus a combination table. SKIPs cleanly (exit 0) when the tree is mid-build (internal/settled-tree-gate.mjs) or pray.doxa.life is unreachable — never reports a false defect from a torn tree. Spawns its own internal/serve-strict.mjs on PORT (default 4180) so it does not depend on another process's server. run `verify:interop:self-test` for the NEGATIVE test.
//scripts.verify:interop:self-test: TWO regression modes, each required to fire ITS OWN combination-named failure: grid-prop-drop (default — freezes the grid child's filter props/attrs on the live dashboard-plus-grid page, reproducing the exact historical bug "selecting anything in the dashboard above did not filter the grid below") and `verify:interop:self-test:camera-freeze` (pins fitBounds/flyTo to no-ops on window.__rdashMap, reproducing "the grid->map link stops moving the camera"). A harness that has only ever reported PASS is unproven.
//scripts.verify:interop:self-test:camera-freeze: ★ A DEDICATED ENTRY, not a mode appended at the call site. The parent script value ends in an inline # comment, so a mode appended by the caller lands INSIDE that comment and the shell drops it — the run then exits 0 in DEFAULT mode, indistinguishable from the mode being selected. A self-test is the proof a gate can fail, so a self-test whose mode cannot be chosen is a gate certifying itself. This entry hardcodes its mode, so nothing has to be appended. (Flag names are deliberately not spelled here: check:script-flags scans script VALUES, and naming one in prose reads as advertising it.)
